fact: Tom Allen came from England to America in July 1867; his first residence in America was Cleveland, Ohio, where he kept a saloon.
Tom Allen settled in St. Louis around 1868.
Tom Allen was a tenant of the same real estate firm since 1868, in different parts of the city.
Tom Allen and Charlie Gallagher were both of Cleveland, Ohio in early 1869.
Tom Allen's arrival in St. Louis was announced a few days before 11 January 1869, and he went out on the Gravois road, some nine miles from the city, to train under Tom Kelly.
Tom Allen and his trainer Tom Kelly boarded the Henry Adkins at Venice on 12 January 1869 on the way to the Davis fight.
Tom Allen boarded the Galatea at Bissell's Point on 23 February 1869 to travel down the river to a fight.
Tom Allen was training at the Buckeye House near Cincinnati for his fight with Mike McCoole in May 1869, having been expected there on 8 May and having left St. Louis for Cincinnati on 10 May.
Tom Allen returned to St. Louis instead of going on to Cincinnati, in response to a telegram, in June 1869.
Tom Allen left Cincinnati on 10 June 1869 after finishing training, and was due to arrive in St. Louis on Saturday 12 June; by 15 June he was reported as supposed to be at Venice.
Tom Allen and Jim Coyne were to go from Cincinnati to Louisville in early July 1869 and return to St. Louis; Allen had spent a few days in Cincinnati with his old English sweetheart.
Tom Allen came into St. Louis on the evening of 13 August 1869 from his training quarters.
Tom Allen, Charley Gallagher and Mike McCoole were permanent residents of St. Louis in August 1869.
Tom Allen and Charley Gallagher were both to go to the fight on 17 August 1869 on the same excursion steamer, joining it at some point beyond the city.
Tom Allen of St. Louis was visiting New York City in September 1869.
Tom Allen's party was expected to be joined by Jem Mace and to reach St. Louis on Saturday 25 September 1869.
Tom Allen reached Cincinnati on 11 October 1869, planning to stay until after his fight with McCoole, and was staying at the Buckeye House there, where crowds came to see him.
On January 25, 1870, Tom Allen was one of the party on the steamer Lady Pike, on an excursion from St. Louis to Carroll Island, Illinois.
Tom Allen was a resident of St. Louis in March 1870.
In May 1870 Tom Allen went to New Orleans to engage Jem Mace, with Joe Coburn expected to travel with him, and returned to St. Louis on May 23 with Mace's agent Abrahams.
Tom Allen had completed an eastern tour and was expected back in St. Louis on July 2, 1870.

In early June 1871 Tom Allen went with Jem Mace's party to Kansas City for the Mace-Coburn fight, arriving with Mace, Dick Hollywood and Jim Cusick on June 1, and went to Westford on June 2, where Joe Coburn did not appear.
Tom Allen said he had returned to St. Louis from the Mace-Coburn fight the day before, in early December 1871.
Tom Allen gave 417 Washington Avenue, St. Louis, as his address in January 1872, and in 1873 his house at that address was to be the place for a match deposit.
On September 1, 1872, Tom Allen left St. Louis for Detroit with Jack Looney and two or three others to see the Mace and O'Baldwin fight.
Tom Allen and Mike McCoole were both residents of St. Louis in 1873, the year Allen beat McCoole.

Tom Allen trained at the Eight-Mile House before his October 1873 fight with Ben Hogan, left for the fighting ground on October 26, and was back in St. Louis on the night of October 28, after the fight failed.
Tom Allen arrived in Kansas City on November 3, 1873 with Arthur Chambers, worked near Omaha, and left Omaha for Kansas City on November 21 after Omaha men threatened to shoot him and Jack Looney.
In 1874 Tom Allen went from St. Louis to Springfield, Illinois, for the dedication of the National Lincoln Monument and the Army of the Tennessee reunion.
In February 1874 Tom Allen was said to propose a speculating tour of his native country, which was the cause of the anticipated match with Jem Mace.
On February 19, 1874, Tom Allen said he had come to St. Louis to live and meant to stay there.
On August 15, 1874, Tom Allen returned to St. Louis from the Edwards-Collyer fight near Pittsburg, Pennsylvania.

In March 1875 Tom Allen went East, arriving in Newark, meeting Jim Coyne, and going on to New York as Harry Hill's guest, and returned to St. Louis on March 19 after visiting the principal Eastern cities.
Tom Allen trained near Pittsburg for his fight with George Rooke in May and June 1875, with Arthur Chambers, and left Pittsburg on June 18 to return to St. Louis.
Tom Allen was living in St. Louis in June 1875.
In autumn 1875 Tom Allen was living a quiet life on Washington Avenue in St. Louis.
On November 17, 1875, Tom Allen arrived in Chicago from St. Louis and planned to stay a couple of days after the match was made.
Tom Allen trained for the Goss fight at a point beyond Carthage.
After the Goss fight and his bonds, Tom Allen got away through Canada and left for England in 1876.
In April 1876 Tom Allen was engaged at the Chicago Adelphi and was there by April 17, as he had said he would be.
Tom Allen left Chicago on the evening of Wednesday, April 26, 1876, for St. Louis, but did not come back with Bauer on April 27 as had been expected.
In late April 1876 Tom Allen's permanent home was reported as Chicago, and Fred Watkins thought he would keep living in St. Louis.

Tom Allen arrived in St. Louis from Cincinnati on May 1, 1876, where he had gone to cover Joe Goss's forfeit money, and was living in St. Louis in May 1876; he repeated that he would continue to live there.
Tom Allen returned to St. Louis in June 1876 and began systematic training under Jack Madden, and Otto Burbank announced he would again make his headquarters in St. Louis after the Goss fight.
Tom Allen and Jack Madden left St. Louis for Cincinnati at the end of their Comique engagement in early July 1876.
Tom Allen and Joe Goss stayed the night before their September 1876 fight at the Gibson House in Cincinnati, and Allen had already left for the fighting ground.
After his release on September 11, 1876, Tom Allen left Covington, Kentucky, for Cincinnati in a carriage with three friends.
Tom Allen returned to St. Louis after the Goss fight in September 1876, registered at the Olive Street hotel, and went to Tom Kelly's saloon at No. 9 North Ninth Street to shake hands with Kelly.
Tom Allen and Jem Mace arrived in St. Louis on October 23, 1876, from an extended sparring tour through the Northeast.
Some people believed Tom Allen's November 1876 flight was meant to take him to the Pacific coast, beyond the reach of his Kentucky prosecutors.
Tom Allen was living in Toronto, Canada, in February 1877.
In March 1877 Tom Allen was in Canada, out of the way of those with warrants, after leaving the young men who had put up his bail.
Tom Allen returned to England in May 1877, planning only a brief stay.
By September 1877 Tom Allen had turned up in London, according to newspaper reports.
Tom Allen was in England in 1878 on a visit to his native country, and ceremonies were held in London in his honour on May 22, 1878.
In late 1878 Tom Allen was reported to be thinking of returning to America and St. Louis.
Tom Allen was expected to cross the Atlantic from England in May 1879 to contest John Dwyer's claim to the title.
Tom Allen, formerly of St. Louis, was living in London, England, in June and November 1879.
For about 23 years Tom Allen lived alone in apartments above his saloon.
Tom Allen was living in England in early 1882, reportedly in Birmingham, and took part in St. George's Day celebrations there.

Tom Allen returned to America from England in 1882 after about six years there, arriving in Boston in October, where he stayed as the guest of Patsy Sheppard at his sporting resort on Hayward Place with his backer; he and his backer were to leave Boston for New York the next day.
W. E. Harding was to go to Chicago with Tom Allen on Saturday to arrange the match with Elliott, and Allen arrived in Chicago on December 13, 1882, having stopped at Pittsburgh on the way.
Tom Allen was rumoured to be on his way to the Saturday night sparring at Tom Kelley's parlors on December 16, 1882, but did not appear.
Tom Allen returned to St. Louis on December 29, 1882, after about six years away, and planned to live there permanently.
Tom Allen attended a quoits game between Dr. Truman of St. Louis and G. Knowles at Sam Swancut's in West Belleville on April 8, 1883.
Tom Allen arrived in St. Louis on the same train as C. A. Booth, a bicyclist who claimed to be champion, in May 1883.
Tom Allen went to Chicago with Tom Kelly in May 1886 to watch the Jack Burke v. Charley Mitchell fight.
Allen and the other men arrested in the Franklin County prize-fight case left St. Louis by train on the evening of April 18, 1888 for a preliminary hearing at Union, Franklin County.
In late 1888 Tom Allen was living in St. Louis 'after a fashion'.

Tom Allen went to New Orleans from St. Louis with a party of sporting men for the Sullivan-Kilrain fight, stayed at the St. Charles Hotel, and was seen taking a lemonade in its rotunda on July 7, 1889; a retrospective account says he went with the St. Louis crowd to the fight at Richburg, Mississippi, in July 1889.

On September 16, 1889 Tom Allen, Dan Daly, Artie Flint, Tom Kelly and Ed Kelly boarded a Wabash train at the Union Depot in St. Louis for Troy, Lincoln County, Mo., to stand trial, and took the 4 o'clock train home from Troy the same day.
Tom Allen was among St. Louis sporting men preparing to go to New Orleans for the Dempsey-Fitzsimmons fight the following Wednesday night.
Tom Allen had been a resident of St. Louis for years.

Tom Allen went to New Orleans with Frank Slavin, and he chaperoned a party of wealthy St. Louisans including his backer Fred Watkins to the Maher-Fitzsimmons fight; he was in the audience at the Olympic Club on March 2, 1892 and arrived home in St. Louis on the night of March 4.
According to the Chicago Mail, Tom Allen was keeping very quiet in St. Louis in June 1892.
Tom Allen left St. Louis for New Orleans for the Sullivan-Corbett fight with his old backer Fred Watkins and friends, and arrived there on Sunday, September 4, 1892 with a large St. Louis delegation.
Tom Allen arrived in New Orleans in March 1893 to second Ed Smith in his coming contest with Joe Goddard.

Tom Allen planned to go to Jacksonville, Florida, to help prepare Charley Mitchell for his fight with Corbett, and was at Mitchell's training quarters on Anastasia Island near St. Augustine in January 1894.
Tom Allen returned to St. Louis from Jacksonville, Florida, by the L. & N. railroad on January 27, 1894, and was the only St. Louis sporting man to make the trip home that day.
Tom Allen was a resident of St. Louis in February 1894.
Tom Allen lived upstairs over his Champion's Rest saloon in March 1895.

In February 1896 Tom Allen had planned to go to Mexico to see the Maher-Fitzsimmons fight, but stayed home after Jim Hall wrote that he would be a sucker to risk his money on the same deal as at Hot Springs; he was one of the St. Louis pugilists quoted in February 1896.
Tom Allen went to New York to see the Peter Maher and Joe Choynski fight and then returned home.
In January 1903 Tom Allen was lying sick at his home on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh.
In March 1903 Tom Allen lived over his saloon at 619 Market Street.
